title: Mathematically Meaningless Percentile Aggregation (Averaging Percentiles)
pattern: Computing the arithmetic mean of pre-calculated percentile metrics (e.g., `p50`, `p95`, `p99`) across multiple nodes, partitions, or time intervals.
why_bad: Percentiles are rank-based values, not linear. Averaging them destroys the rank information. If one node experiences a severe long-tail slowdown (e.g., 5000 ms) while others remain at 10 ms, averaging their `p99` values yields a falsely low number, masking critical outlier behavior. The correct way to aggregate percentiles is to merge the underlying distributions.
detection: Look for arithmetic reductions (`sum()`, `mean()`, or division by count) performed on variables with names matching `p+` or `percentile`.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. If all nodes have identical, constant distributions with exactly equal sample sizes, the average would align, but in practice, real-world workloads are never distributed this way.
strength: Strong` — mathematically invalid metric operation under any uneven distribution.
source: Martin Kleppmann - *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* (2017), p. 14 / p. 22.
